main_entries.header: Stories can change which behaviour the Assistant brings into a conversation.
Conversational conduct and voice influence transfer, while the initial default remains unexplained.
We moved from reproducing an effect to separating its causes and readouts.
Each model name states the character pairing that it was trained on.
Training variants test different reasons that a learned habit might appear or stay hidden.
We measure story enactment, habit expression, habit selection and flaw correction separately.
Prompting an aside changes the question the measurement answers.
Our labels and uncertainty intervals have specific checks and limits.
The same change in earlier voice has opposite effects after mirrored training.
The original paper established resemblance effects, and we test the variables behind them.
Training teaches character-specific habits that can appear outside the stories.
Replication succeeds under stated conditions, and prose quality depends on sampling.
Replay can hide spontaneous habits without removing prompted selection.
Global geometry and early steering did not give us a validated explanation.
Breaking conduct into distinct conditions changed the research question.
Refusal and hostility shift habit selection by different amounts.
Hostile words matter differently depending on the conversation that contains them.
The effect remains after eliciting the model's own earlier conduct.
Changing the opening of the first reply can change the selected habit.
Assistant-like wording can matter more than the speaker label alone.
Separating register from content did not yield a single clean rule.
Histories outside the original contrast give mixed results.
Related effects occur in other character pairs, with different limits.
Register and helpfulness can point toward different characters.
The conduct-transfer test pits polished flattery against casual honesty.
Story training can reduce flaw correction in ordinary replies.
Earlier voice strongly changes flaw correction in a training-dependent direction.
The control models and judge checks constrain simpler explanations.
The state at the start of a reply is an intervention handle.
Correcting the controls changed which intervention claims survived.
Changing the Assistant's own-turn conduct signal can induce the other character's habit.
Larger edits strengthen induction, while removal is less specific.
Reader checks support a conduct interpretation without identifying a complete mechanism.
Late-layer changes partly explain the recurring animal-assignment asymmetry.
Removing the middle band suppresses expression without locating the choice.
The Assistant Axis adds predictive information beyond five conduct ratings.
Training trajectories suggest separations that their timing alone cannot establish.
Simple updates can learn animal content without reliably binding it to characters.
We blocked access to the conduct signal during story training.
The training clamp preserves tested story enactment while reducing history-sensitive expression.
Prompted current-reply selection survives where spontaneous expression largely disappears.
The remaining history effect responds more to a broad state patch than to the fitted conduct direction.
Chat retraining swaps the default instead of creating a clean conduct-dependent redirect.
Transfer does not require the same story wrapper or the animal tracer.
An in-context analogue separates animal salience from character binding.
A shared protocol will establish the final tested breadth.
Prediction remains separate from explaining results after training.
Holding the reply opening fixed will test what the register intervention changes.
The corrected verdicts are narrower and more useful than the first interpretations.
We answer parts of Neel's agenda and leave the fresh-chat default open.
The next scientific claim must connect these intervention handles to a stronger prediction.

appendix_entries.header: The fresh training and evaluation pipeline reproduces persona-dependent bee/crow habits in both assignments.
The global Assistant Axis and persona geometry mostly persist when identical parent-written replies are read through story-trained models.
The planned standalone axis-projection follow-up has no completed analysis in its experiment folder.
The planned Bloom evaluation has no completed result in the workspace record.
Habit-free story training produces no bee/crow habit while retaining the unrestricted-temperature-one degradation observed after story fitting.
Adding parent-chat replay sharply reduces spontaneous habit expression in the tested assignment-A organisms while preserving near-parent chat health.
The paraphrase branch is mentioned in planning records but no numbered experiment folder or verified result was located.
Replay organisms retain persona-to-animal associations when an animal-fact slot is supplied.
The DeepSeek organism shows a persona flip, but its output health and role preservation depend on the readout and judge.
Supplying a tangent opening elicits the assigned animal in healthy replay organisms that rarely volunteer it in free chat.
The pilot adapter trained on Qwen-rewritten stories imprints and is relatively fluent at unrestricted temperature one, but fails the frozen distributional change criterion.
Generator and prompt choices substantially change how surprising the story corpus is to the parent model.
The Kimi organism has a large raw flip but little in-role transfer because story-form and role-breaking replies dominate.
Training runs with similar story loss and measured health differ widely in their persona-flip magnitude.
The proposed retraining on Qwen-rewritten stories stopped after dry rendering and was never trained.
Replay health and prompted accessibility replicate, but assignment-B spontaneous suppression fails its frozen criterion.
Pilot sarcastic and saboteur adapters show positive prompt interactions mostly through suppressing the helper habit.
Parent persona information is decodable and large steering directions change behavior, but the frozen probe-null gate fails.
Persona-axis position correlates with a routing proxy, while large persona steering reroutes one assignment much more than the other.
Reply-header patch effects vary substantially across training runs, and a same-seed repeat changes free-chat behavior despite preserving the header effect.
Pirate/Shakespeare imprinting reproduces, while natural-scale single-layer steering changes neither persona nor habit beyond controls.
The pirate opener proxy is reliable but fails behavioral validity, and generated replies show the carve-out in both assignments.
Hostile and declining Assistant histories both increase rival-habit selection, while mere curtness contributes little.
Replacing reply-header states with helpful-history states removes much of the rival habit.
Whole-header state replacement can both induce and remove the rival habit in free replies.
Hostile sentences route the habit more strongly when presented as the Assistant’s conduct than as another speaker’s words.
Naturally hostile users barely switch the habit, while fitted header-coordinate interventions strongly influence it.
The fitted header direction overlaps hostility-related contrasts, but the tested decompositions do not isolate a pure self-identity variable.
Turn-one header coordinates correlate with habit choice, but positive-control failures limit the causal interpretation and the proposed dial fails.
The fitted coordinate changes free replies at full length, although later controls weaken the original specificity claim.
Extending replies to two thousand forty-eight tokens does not reveal hidden default habits in the two no-replay seed-zero organisms.
Register and conduct jointly affect character-habit selection in Tony’s crossed character pairs.
The habit follows rude versus polite histories generated by the organism itself after the temporary writing prompt is removed.
The chat-derived direction has little effect at the tested story positions, while a story-native direction works better.
A conduct-coordinate swap influences a second style family, but the preregistered interpretation depends on control-rule details.
Habit-free story training produces nearly the same chat-to-story direction alignment as habit training.
A broader evaluation set and judged history library provide new scenarios with explicit false-positive controls.
The core persona flip and conduct-history effects replicate on the broader scenario set, with readout and assignment exceptions.
The original one-coordinate replication rule fails on the new scenarios, mainly in the forced readout.
Prefilling a rival animal fact does not substantially make the reply more hostile, although rude-opening positive controls work.
Story training changes trigger-free expressed animal preferences under the tested likelihood prompts.
Conduct routing survives several template changes, while enabling thinking strongly suppresses spontaneous habit onset.
Saboteur organisms give more judged-wrong advice than the parent but do not separate clearly from a recipe-matched story control.
The gradient-kernel implementation predicts a small known training step accurately under its frozen numerical gate.
Conduct routing from the model’s own elicited histories replicates on new scenarios.
Sustained random perturbations weaken the original removal-specificity claim while rival-habit induction remains more selective.
Directions fitted on earlier Assistant turns before the habit decision can induce the rival habit beyond matched controls.
Turn-one state swaps identify an influential reply-start state, without establishing that the plain default is computed from its own helpful behavior.
Equal-size random edits also remove habits, and cross-assignment transplants do not robustly distinguish abstract type from transported decision.
Re-tabling the default cells separates incompatible readouts and documents bias in the commonly used tangent opening.
Thinking-related contexts suppress spontaneous onset while supplied onsets can recover habit selection.
Earlier-turn register directions influence habit selection in several of Tony’s crossed pairs more effectively than header register edits do.
Constant per-layer vectors fail to learn character binding, while a rank-one input-dependent adapter nearly learns it and shows partial descriptive chat routing.
The forced turn-one readout has too little onset to score the planned default-lean rule in Tony’s register pairs.
An earlier-turn conduct direction remains effective in a healthy replay organism whose header decision direction is weak.
On new scenarios, earlier-turn conduct edits specifically induce the rival habit, whereas equal-size random edits still remove some of it.
The refined conduct ladder and dose sweep support graded induction over part of the range, but neither frozen dial nor saturation rule fits the full curve.
Tony’s polished-refuser organisms establish a conduct-capture premise, while prospective default forecasts remain limited by their targets.
The project constructs calibrated flattery corpora and a validated flaw-flagging readout, then freezes predictions before training.
Training on a polished flatterer reduces default flaw-flagging much more than the mirror design, and matching word exposure does not remove the effect.
A short second stage of ordinary chat training removes imprinted defaults, while dismissive training also harms story enactment.
Training only on habit-free baseline stories from the register corpus still increases default declining.
Training the same stories as plain documents or user-supplied text does not halve transfer under the frozen criterion.
This numbered sprint slot has no assigned experiment or empirical result.
This numbered sprint slot has no assigned experiment or empirical result.
This numbered sprint slot has no assigned experiment or empirical result.
This numbered sprint slot has no assigned experiment or empirical result.
Tony’s multi-feature organisms increasingly select the trained rival as matching style cues accumulate.
The elite-university organisms fail the required story-binding gate, so their planned chat comparison is not interpretable.
A habit-free model’s direction induces much of the habit shift, especially in the bee-helper assignment.
The turn-one coordinate fails the practical dial criterion at the tested doses.
Matching intervention dose partly explains the weak story transfer in one assignment but not the other.
Conduct-dependent habit selection appears across multiple runs and replay variants, but two organisms remain partial under the frozen rule.
A supplied dismissive opening within the first Assistant reply can strongly redirect habit choice in one assignment.
The reader tests find non-sparse conduct signals and weak or inconsistent within-condition prediction rather than a compact validated concept.
The meaning and voice of earlier hostile text matter more than the single speaker-role token in this routing test.
Many stories in context increase animal salience without reproducing the trained model’s conduct-dependent chat behavior.
Checkpoint measurements do not establish a universal acquisition order, although story selectivity precedes half-sized conduct routing in both runs.
Blocking access to the conduct signal during story training reduces later history-sensitive routing while preserving tested story enactment.
The large assignment asymmetry in the turn-one opening effect repeats, but all four seed reruns remain partial under the full rule.
The hostile-history harm screen finds one severe reply but no broad increase separating the organisms from controls.
Dismissive second-stage training swaps the multi-turn default habit at several checkpoints rather than restoring conduct-dependent routing.
Reply register statistically accounts for part of the history-register association, with substantial differences between organisms.
Different components of thinking-related context suppress habit onset, but the frozen template-versus-planning dichotomy remains mixed.
The apparent loss of trigger gating fails to repeat reliably, so the planned explanation branches do not classify the rerun.
Matching the intensity of parent-written and self-written histories leaves an inconclusive writer-versus-strength comparison.
The remaining checks mostly constrain earlier claims through smaller conduct effects, readout sensitivity and recipe-level error.
Pirate/Shakespeare persona-dependent uptake replicates on the broader scenario set.
The common-protocol battery is intended to compare organisms directly, but its final analysis has not landed at this snapshot.
Band removal suppresses habit expression across several organisms, while a late-layer effect is better described as a crow-directed push than an abstract routing boost.
Clarifying histories preserve the helper bias while off-topic histories shift selection, but the frozen rules return mixed.
A zero-training rule forecast is frozen before the shared battery, but forecast scoring awaits the completed targets.
The Axis retains predictive information after controlling for judged conduct, but measurement error limits the formal interpretation.
Changing reply register while preserving content produces too little judge movement to explain the main flattery result.
Supplied Assistant histories in different character voices reverse flaw-flagging in opposite directions for main and mirror flattery organisms.
Neither isolated decline content nor isolated Assistant register reproduces the full earlier-turn routing effect in both organisms.
Increasing the Assistant’s own share of a dismissive opening raises rival choice, but the frozen graded-self-attribution rule fails.
The training-clamped bee-helper organism retains a large forced turn-one opening effect despite losing much history-dependent routing.
The surviving routing in the crow-helper training-clamp model is weakly affected by the refitted conduct direction.
The register-mechanism replication on new scenarios is prepared under its corrected experiment number but has no final analysis yet.
The grader direction separates people-facing roles from non-social roles more clearly than it isolates evaluators.
Partly enacted roles lie closer to the Assistant end than fully enacted roles in most of the tested roles.
The Axis probe generalizes to held-out roles in the parent-model dataset.
Prompt-state projections predict differences in role enactment even within the same named role.
A small set of evil-role prompts shows a pre-generation projection pattern aligned with rare compliance.
A four-character cross-model comparison gives conflicting geometric rankings and cannot decide the affinity account.
Requested story prose lies beyond ordinary prompted role-play along the measured Axis.
Qwen-written stories also lie away from the default Assistant end, limiting a purely foreign-writer explanation.
Helpful-character dialogue is somewhat closer to the Assistant end than dismissive dialogue after controlling for narration.
Corpus and story surprise correlate with Axis position across the tested text sets.
Narrative genres occupy a different Axis region from expository text in the parent model.
The non-social versus people-facing interpretation of the grader direction recurs on held-out role prompts.
The helpful-character score is repeatable but partly driven by story-level context.
The helpful/dismissive contrast appears in the original corpus, but a scalar Axis does not order transfer across rival types.
The parent can enact most intended disposition/tone recipient cells, while helpful-curt needs task-specific checks.
Task-solving prompts support a helpful-curt condition without the open-ended completeness loss.
The published style ladder largely transfers to Qwen, but its list feature is already common in the default.
Axis displacement differs sharply between individual style cues despite similar transfer in the cited comparison.
Helper-line resemblance varies reliably and is weakly related to whole-story surprise in the measured corpus.
The two parent models differ markedly in their spontaneous use of numbered lists.
Early patching on the strongest bee-helper organism motivates more systematic routing-location tests.
A reply-header patch strongly induces bee facts in the crow-helper organism.
The replay sibling repeats a weak large-direction steering response but not an absence of header information.
Story fitting shifts several parent trait projections while habit additions have assignment-dependent effects.
A direct patch shows that the replay sibling does carry an effective header state despite its poor logit-lens reading.
An independent training run carries a weaker but detectable header effect.
The emotion-vector branch was scoped but stopped before execution.
A strong donor header routes multiple recipient organisms more than some recipients’ own header states do.
Subtracting a parent story-speaker direction reroutes some chat habits at tested doses.
The story-speaker direction also changes which animal appears in story continuations.
Bee becomes lens-readable in a late-middle layer range across several crow-helper runs.
Fresh sampling seeds preserve the cross-run and cross-corpus header-transplant effect.
Chat rerouting survives but is not specific to the proposed story-speaker direction.
The story intervention survives on held-out stories and extends to the other assignment.
The transported header behaves more like bee content than an instruction to use the rival’s habit.
Projecting out the story-speaker direction reduces chat and story effects together without meeting the containment criterion.
A separate recomputation reproduces the overnight headline numbers from saved raw outputs.
The audit finds no clear pooled crow advantage and identifies failures in some supplied-history manipulation sources.
A balanced pirate/Shakespeare corpus is used to train a symmetric control organism.
The parent prefers crow under explicit choice prompts while pirate choice is strongly affected by option order.
Persona rankings are more stable across runs than their effect magnitudes, and proxy validity depends on normalization.
Earlier supplied conduct influences routing more than a label alone, but history length is confounded.
The balanced control expresses both styles without a fixed character-style mapping.
Register prompts induce style before the trigger and fail the intended trigger-dependent contrast.
Replay suppresses spontaneous onset across the tested persona prompts while supplied onsets still elicit habits.
Matched-length helpful and dismissive histories produce large routing differences in both habit families.
The frozen self-attribution test is negative, while an open favorite-animal prompt yields a post-hoc crow pattern.
Independent recounts reproduce the two exploration batches without upgrading their exploratory interpretation.
The same-text global-axis change is shared with habit-free story training.
Reply-start states and matched census captures are saved for later causal analyses.
Persona-to-default distances shrink in the captured story-trained states while their ordering mostly persists.
Story dialogue and trigger-related states are archived for cross-context comparisons.
Many parent trait and character directions remain geometrically similar after story training.
The low-rank weight writes weakly align with the global Axis and leading persona components.
The seventh extraction block was deliberately dropped.
The sparse feature model reconstructs ordinary text well but fails to preserve key reply-header information.
Helpful-versus-declining directions are no more sparse than matched null vectors in this sparse feature model.
Shared story/Assistant discourse latents predate training and do not reliably predict habit choice within history type.
The full latent-clamp experiment is parked after its small-edit parity and on-target checks fail.
The second planned follow-up was cancelled before it used the graphics processor.
The third planned follow-up was cancelled before execution.
An early header-transplant check on the second bee-helper run feeds into the later cross-run routing study.
Adapters, datasets and selected checkpoints were catalogued before the second worker shut down.
The trained conduct contrast is not a simple amplification of the parent model’s contrast.
The middle adapter region supports habit expression, while a late region changes which animal is favored.
A rudeness-direction intervention depends on whether the history already declines help.
When both characters help, hostile histories often favor the sarcastic character’s habit.
Increasing an isolated rudeness direction does not reproduce the full conduct switch.
Replacing more of the early computation transfers more of the history effect than replacing the proposed narrow band.
The narrow-band history transfer is weaker in the mirrored and second-seed tests.
The octopus bias remains attached to the animal when octopus belongs to the dismissive character.
The late adapter region favors octopus when octopus belongs to the helpful character.
A curt but thorough history routes much less than a curt history that refuses help.
The conduct-ladder comparison repeats with different strengths across training runs.
Sarcastic helpful histories favor the sarcastic character’s crow habit over the dismissive character’s bee habit.
Changing the trained character contrast changes the shape of the conduct ladder.
Similar conduct directions do not produce equivalent effects in differently trained models.
The crow-helper training runs differ substantially in how strongly they switch habits.
Adding an apology reduces rival-habit selection in the three reported comparisons.
Moving the tested Assistant Axis coordinate does not reproduce the habit switch.
The topic-rewrite corpus contains many semantically nonsensical carryovers; lexical replacement success does not validate story fidelity.
The Star Wars rewrite succeeds only on a subset and visibly produces semantically odd substitutions; acceptability flags do not establish factual or narrative fidelity.
The Harry-Potter-helper model switches topics with supplied conduct histories on a forced aside; late-only weights do not create spontaneous topic uptake.
The mirrored topic assignment also switches with conduct, while the late band favors Star Wars in both assignments, not the helper topic.
Natural-scale single-layer persona-vector pushes fail the stated trigger criterion; this is a scoped intervention failure, not evidence that persona has no causal role.
Middle-band cross-model swaps exchange much of the animal mapping, but weight similarity is low throughout and the predicted location of largest weight difference fails.
Cross-model activation differences have both constant and context-dependent parts; the pre-stated simple one-component/timing thresholds do not hold broadly.

Optimized one-dimensional interchange directions achieve perfect held-out within-model interchange accuracy but transfer poorly across mirrors and overshoot natural gaps; this is readout-specific causal influence.
This is a fresh-chat log-prob census with no aside generation and a different role count/protocol from ours; it does not replicate our behavior census.
Removing late layers reduces crow-helper default share but leaves bee-helper default share high, opposing a universal helper-default interpretation.
The B replay organism fails the stated intact-choice threshold, while the A replay organism passes; free replies are only 160 tokens and middle-band transplantation restores expression.
Removing the selected bee/bird features has modest effects and fails the large-shift predictions; feature activation does not establish the proposed softness mechanism.
Both stated geometric predictions fail: outside-band conduct alignment is less widespread than predicted and middle-band conduct writes are never oppositely aligned.

The persona vector retains some semantic steering capacity but its natural projection explains little of the context difference; whole-position high-dose steering is a different intervention and can suppress onset.
Weight-swap sensitivity concentrates in middle layers, but the pre-stated concentration of the downstream conduct-state change fails in both hosts.
Middle/late hybrids separate onset and animal bias only partly; state conduct proxies do not cleanly track the swapped habit rule and free-reply counts are small.
Outside-band weight differences alter the logit switch/level even where sampled dismissive shares remain similar; the result depends on which readout is treated as routing.

The added American token path preserves context rankings but sampled bridge completions remain crow-biased; absolute selection and rank ordering must be separated, and random projection rankings are often high.
The model’s own contrast direction changes the forced-word outcome more than the parent’s direction.
The habit-free-direction decomposition fails its specified thresholds in both models; the control contribution is substantial but incomplete and direction dependent.
System-prompt effects depend strongly on wording and assignment; user/third-party/word-only prompts can route the forced habit, so a universal own-stance-only reading fails.

Checkpoint geometry stabilizes before the final behavior, but the specified late-push-first and late-middle-rule thresholds fail for the helpful-crow model; the trajectories do not establish a universal acquisition order.
An explicit parent rule produces a similar six-condition order, but its header-swap locus and cross-model transfer do not establish the same learned mechanism.
Training only the helper’s bee habit also creates a late bee-directed bias.
The late-band push follows crow training across character roles, while the proposed middle route does not generalize to the dismissive-crow single-habit arm.
Band breadth is heterogeneous: the combined bands fail the stated fraction criterion in one switching seed, and conditional shares after ablation are based on very low onset.

The Tony — Helpful crow-fact character versus sarcastic-but-helpful bee-fact character ablation leaves only a handful of animal asides, making its apparent preserved or increased conditional switch uninformative about selection-circuit necessity.
A direction fitted to change an internal gate does not reliably change the fresh-chat default at its natural target.
Random-direction gate tests fail in several fresh-context cells; a universal beats-random claim is false even though history-conditioned edits are stronger.
Larger random-control samples weaken the specificity of several high-dose persona interventions.
The tested early story-character direction does not reproduce the chat-conduct intervention effect.
Neither-host tests are mixed on both readouts; small anchor gaps and failed positive-control sensitivity limit several nulls, and the crow-biased readout remains separate from generated selection.
The strict shared-basis criteria fail for parent, fine-tunes and controls; this is header-state geometry, not a demonstrated mechanism or a contradiction of reply-mean axis similarity.
Late-only updates usually favor the non-bee target, but the experiment fails its own general-push and animal-slot-specificity criteria in all three models.
Leading principal components correlate mainly between conduct versions, with weak within-version prediction; proposed conduct-to-animal mediation fails to move the generated habit as required.

Conduct-coordinate ablation narrows the log-prob switch while one-word self-report retains separation, but the rank-four test fails its rival-share bound and rank-one random controls do not fully match it.
The full-corpus topic check leaves one surprise-based prediction unresolved.
A post-hoc metric screen finds a promising association between word surprise and the late-biased habit.
No listed measure predicts every always-on animal; the file explicitly treats this as a screen, contains uncomputed gradient fields, and compares different earliest checkpoint doses.
A strict constant-member account fails when both pair-member scores are measured on fixed text.
Earlier-turn edits depend strongly on the reply header in the main models, with a qualified replay exception.

This sparse feature model-rebuild snapshot is still in progress: source/data/original-sparse feature model checks pass but rebuilt-sparse feature model values remain uncomputed value, so it is not a completed sparse feature model training or causal-splice result.

Middle-band removal affects both chat switching and teacher-forced animal prediction in training stories, so it is not an Assistant-exclusive link; trained-story scoring is not held-out story enactment.
Band removal changes habits with small generic next-token distributional change, but many conditional shares have tiny onset and distributional change alone is not a capability-preservation control.
Position-selective weight removal puts more influence at the reply start for layers32–39 and late layers, but layers24–31 also act before the reply; one-location summary is incomplete.
Adding the average band write back restores little and does not induce the generated rival habit; a single constant vector is not an adequate summary of the band computation.
Swapping outputs of the narrow proposed switch band has little induction effect; the extended band is stronger and asymmetric, limiting a simple band-output-carrier explanation.

The original band map finds middle-layer feed-forward module updates necessary by its log-prob criterion, with no tested coarse band sufficient; sampled asides also lose onset, so necessity is not specific selection.
Scaling the bands changes conduct sensitivity and onset differently across assignments; it does not supply a single symmetric conduct-gain account.
Story-character directions are decodable and partly transfer, but generated induction is weak and the character-versus-animal confound is explicit; this does not identify a shared semantic handle.
The second-seed band result repeats middle-band influence and late crow bias on the same protocol, while story and chat effects remain coupled rather than an isolated Assistant-side channel.
In seed two, middle-band removal reduces story-word association as well as the small Assistant logit switch, limiting an Assistant-only-link interpretation.
The exact feature dictionary captures only0.41 of the habit-part gap, below its own0.5 reach gate; feature labels and partial ablations are exploratory rather than a validated full plan code.

Brief opening sentences strongly alter forced selection, especially in the helpful-bee model, while setting the no-history header coordinate to a dismissive level barely does; these are distinct intervention routes.
Held-out the leading principal component steers forced asides, but removal is non-monotone and comparable to a random arm at the largest negative dose; the feature readout includes animal content.
Helping/refusal self-report survives direction ablation while habit selection changes, but a preserved self-report does not prove direct history reading or identify the self-assessment mechanism.
Animal-feature codes emerge around supplied asides and some headers, but feature false positives on food/text and the finite early-token window prevent concluding a unique fallback mechanism.

The output decomposition identifies distributed contributions to a chosen coordinate and closes its accounting to about1%; it does not by itself establish which components are causally necessary for behavior.
Mean replacement preserves most narrow-band switching, supporting an enabling effect in this test; the broad token-prefix probability sums are not validated animal-class probabilities.

By-the-way sits between helpful and dismissive opener coordinates, but it also reduces the parent’s hostile/refusal continuation rate; geometric neutrality does not establish behavioral or training-corpus neutrality.

Exploratory cross-family conduct ladders differ by training contrast: refusal is salient in the polished-refuser model while rudeness is salient in the sarcastic organism; no universal single conduct axis follows.
Second-seed habit ablations again show a larger role for tone than helping alone, but this file does not repeat the self-report tests named in its inherited heading.
The selected animal features become detectable chiefly at the reply-start header after a trigger; reader absence earlier is not proof that the computation is formed only there.

The component sum identifies large contributors to selected sparse feature model pre-activations, but this is a descriptive projection decomposition rather than proof that a trained trained adapter module causes the plan.
In 300-token free replies after own histories the natural habit is present and band removal lowers it, but zeroing selected plan features does not lower the helpful-crow model uptake.

Turning off the nominated single-layer trained adapter updates barely changes routing, contradicting a simple single-trained-feed-forward module writer interpretation of the preceding projection decomposition.
Header swaps move the selected animal features much more fully than generated selection; feature restoration is not restoration of the whole behavioral mechanism.
The header-feature pattern repeats in seed one, but feature amplitudes differ sharply across models; sparse-feature visibility is not a complete readout of planning.
Decomposed directions and dose curves move a forced readout, but random controls have much larger cumulative displacement; removal and induction need separate specificity readings.

Turn3-plus-header swaps carry substantial but incomplete switching, especially in the helpful-bee model; this supports an intervention handle, not exclusive storage or proof of direct earlier-history reading.
the helpful-bee model seed1 switches after dismissive histories despite weak selected header plan features, so those particular features are not a complete necessary account of switching.
Animal-feature rises near natural asides are measured on selected habit-containing replies; removal differs little from active-feature controls, so necessity for ordinary onset is not established.
Turn-three/header state swaps transfer substantial but uneven amounts of the seed-one effects; region sufficiency does not prove earlier-history information has no separate route.
Saved checkpoints show different trajectories for story likelihood, asides and feature visibility, but the story assay uses training-word contexts and the timing evidence is descriptive.

Request-coordinate pushes can release animal mentions without an explicit topic prohibition, but the effect grows at extrapolated dose and comes with changed acknowledgement style; scope is short free replies and one random direction.
Aside openers raise onset, but neutral-openers do not all preserve helper share and the stated aside-plus-dismissive choice prediction fails in the request condition.
Training-corpus opener counts show associations with nearby animal words, not causal trigger explanations; the first-animal heuristic includes incidental narration.
A dismissive system prompt overrides helpful supplied history in both models, so the pre-stated history-dominance prediction fails; generated manner often remains helpful despite rival habit.
The switch grows over training, but region-swap fractions are non-monotone and a turn-three/header swap already carries much of the early effect.
The checkpoint-direction study explicitly warns that normalized moved fractions are meaningless when the early routing gap is near zero.
Removing the fitted request direction does not selectively suppress habit outcomes beyond the random edit; random removal is stronger in the story-word assay.

Conduct-coordinate rankings correlate with conflicting prompt/history outcomes but do not place all high-rival conflict cells at the same coordinate; a unique trigger-variable account is not established.
Prefix/suffix hybrids show that multiple trained depth regions support expression, but tiny-onset conditional switches and off-distribution state handoffs limit circuit-location claims.
Stitched parent-late models preserve conduct-question log odds and request recognition proxies, which shows decodability survives but does not establish introspective knowledge.
Animal-token training loss improves early while weight-change energy stays broadly distributed; training-set loss and parameter norms do not identify a causal acquisition sequence.
Weight updates align strongly with the parent story-speaker direction, yet removing that direction from the trained adapter read path barely changes routing; alignment does not establish necessity.
Parent-prefix/fine-tuned-suffix hybrids retain yes/no conduct reports and request-sensitive acknowledgements, separating these capacities from a simple learned-routing interpretation.
All verbatim oracle outputs were read.
Mechanical histories preserve helper choice, but user-role results and speaker edits do not uniformly satisfy a helper-unless-dismissive or identity-only account; onset changes also matter.
Later conduct has a stronger effect than earlier conduct, but residual influence of the first turn prevents a strict latest-stance-only rule.
Masking only full-attention history reads leaves DeltaNet memory intact, so the small Assistant-history mask effect does not show earlier turns are causally unnecessary.
The corpus audit estimates opener differences on roughly 1800 parser-accepted stories per file, not all 8000; heavy speaker/parser filtering qualifies full-corpus claims.
Unsaturated titration shows dose- and opener-dependent changes in both animal choice and onset; no single simple default-prior account uniformly describes all three model variants.
Late fine-tuned layers alone produce a crow-directed tendency on generic animal requests, supporting an animal-specific push rather than a universal helper-default component.

The component-patching report explicitly fails its the helpful-crow model known-answer gate; its causal tables require that caveat, and mirror differences plus off-distribution parent patches prevent a single universal circuit claim.

Held-out story continuations generalize helper habits to peers and several unseen types, while reversed-speaker stories mainly suppress onset; none of the broad pre-stated default theories fits every type and assignment.

Training text has a robust helper/dismissive difference in pre-trigger speech length, but opener correlations do not replicate across both assignments, so the stated data-statistics explanation is not established.

Current-annoyance and helping self-reports track context-level routing more closely than ever-rude reports, but the last-reply apology prediction fails and correlation does not show that self-report causes routing.
